rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Vaccination can prime or expand antigen-reactive cells without normally genetically rewriting the receptors of mature T cells.
rows.entailment: The existing receptor note explicitly distinguishes recruitment or expansion of mature specificities from introduction of engineered receptor sequences.
sourceScope: OpenStax 21.3 clonal-selection/expansion paragraphs; this is the ordinary vaccine mechanism, not an assertion about every possible intervention.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: A conventional T-cell receptor recognizes peptide with HLA; a tumour DNA alteration is an upstream antigen source, not the directly recognized object.
rows.entailment: The receptor paragraph defines peptide-HLA recognition, while the source paragraph makes the DNA alteration an upstream candidate. Together they prevent equating a mutation call with the recognised object.
sourceScope: OpenStax presentation paragraphs and Wells consortium methods; conventional peptide-HLA recognition is the stated scope.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Keep innate sensing and a specific adaptive response distinct.
rows.entailment: The paragraph explicitly identifies innate sensing and specific adaptive responses as interacting but different observations.
sourceScope: OpenStax 42.2 opening and Kranz 2016 abstract; no vaccine efficacy is inferred from innate sensing.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Credible tumour sequences, target selection and product construction are successive questions after the recognition mechanism is understood.
rows.entailment: The source paragraph places understanding recognition before source-list, HLA, selection and construction questions, with the receptor paragraph explaining the mechanism.
sourceScope: A reading framework derived from the guide and the distinct measurements in Wells; not a universal clinical manufacturing protocol.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: A matching receptor can be present at low frequency before antigen exposure; appropriate activation can select and increase responding cells.
rows.entailment: The text names an already matching population, possible low starting frequency and activation/selection in a supporting context.
sourceScope: Textbook clonal selection and expansion; no numerical repertoire size or individual response probability is adopted.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Adult thymic output declines with age but does not cease at a universal twentieth-birthday cutoff; retain the measurement and population scope of the supporting study.
rows.entailment: The existing paragraph describes continued adult output, age-related decline and peripheral maintenance instead of a fixed birthday shutdown.
sourceScope: Douek 1998 abstract: TCR-rearrangement-product measurements, age and HIV-treatment context, with no universal individual export rate or cancer benefit.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: A pre-dose blood sample is a limited comparison, not a complete inventory of every receptor.
rows.entailment: The fictional pre-dose report is explicitly limited to blood sampling and cannot establish absence from blood or the whole body.
sourceScope: Premise-backed sampling inference; not a measured whole-body repertoire census.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Priming denotes initial activation of a naive T cell.
rows.entailment: The existing paragraph defines priming as a naive cell's initial activation, retaining the supporting context.
sourceScope: Established activation teaching; only the definition is used, not a fresh certification of every cytokine experiment in that owner.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Dendritic-cell peptide display and supporting signals contribute to priming.
rows.entailment: Dendritic-cell display and supporting signals are explicitly named as contributions to naive-cell priming.
sourceScope: OpenStax activation context and Kranz abstract; no claim that display alone is sufficient.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Direct presentation after a cell translates vaccine RNA and class-I cross-presentation of acquired antigen are distinct routes.
rows.entailment: The retained paragraph distinguishes direct presentation by an RNA-transfected cell from acquisition/display routes and from naive-cell cross-priming.
sourceScope: Joffre review abstract defines cross-presentation; Kranz abstract supports encoded-antigen expression in dendritic cells. Older cross-dressing details retain their earlier recorded source scope.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: After priming, effector cells still need access to the tumour, a displayed recognized target and functional capacity.
rows.entailment: The paragraph separately requires tumour access, an appropriate displayed target and retained function after priming.
sourceScope: Mechanistic dependency/reading inference, not a promised trafficking rate, killing result or treatment benefit.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: A shared antigen-processing defect can limit several candidate targets, rather than being solved by adding more source sequences.
rows.entailment: The exact sentence states that a shared processing defect can affect several targets and that adding peptide candidates does not bypass it.
sourceScope: Zaretsky 2016 abstract supplies the bounded melanoma B2M/class-I-loss example; no universal defect frequency is claimed.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: The delivery-to-presentation-to-activation-to-access-to-recognition-to-benefit sequence is a set of separately testable dependencies, not a guarantee of killing or durable benefit.
rows.entailment: The text states the priming-to-attack dependencies, rejects a guaranteed or strict timing chain, and requires separate killing and durable-benefit outcomes.
sourceScope: The rendered six-box diagram is read as dependencies. Its vertical order is not evidence that tumour display starts after trafficking.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: A fictional blood peptide-response increase supports a response in the sampled compartment, without establishing tumour entry, natural recognition or recurrence prevention.
rows.entailment: The fictional blood-response example explicitly leaves tumour entry, natural recognition and recurrence prevention unestablished.
sourceScope: An invented worked example interpreted through assay/endpoint distinctions, not a patient cohort.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Repeating a blood count cannot by itself test natural tumour recognition or added clinical efficacy.
rows.entailment: The paragraph says that repeating the blood measurement cannot resolve tumour recognition or the clinical comparison.
sourceScope: A premise-backed measurement rule; no diagnostic sensitivity or causal effect is assigned.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Rare or absent matching cells, inappropriate delivery, inadequate display or supporting signals, and later access/function barriers are different failure modes requiring different measurements.
rows.entailment: Rare or unavailable matching cells, delivery, display/support, access and function are separately named failure modes requiring different measurements.
sourceScope: A mechanism-based failure framework, not measured frequencies or a treatment-selection algorithm.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: A tenfold increase in a sampled receptor sequence reports increased representation; specificity, absolute cell expansion and cancer killing are separate questions.
rows.entailment: The tenfold sequence example is explicitly a representation change, distinct from new specificity, absolute expansion, killing and benefit.
sourceScope: The tenfold value is fictional; no actual cell count or receptor-function assay is supplied.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: In the fictional clone-Q exercise, pre-dose non-detection with a stated 0.1% reliability limit is not proof that Q was absent.
rows.entailment: Non-detection under the fictional 0.1% reliability statement is explicitly not proof of absence.
sourceScope: Fictional compatible-assay premise; 0.1% is not a clinical threshold or an exact upper confidence bound.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: A later 1% frequency supports first detection and possible enrichment, but an unmeasured baseline does not supply an exact observed fold change.
rows.entailment: The post-dose 1% result earns first detection/possible enrichment but no exact observed fold change from an unmeasured baseline.
sourceScope: Fictional sampling and denominator assumptions; nominal 1/0.1 is not an observed baseline-to-follow-up fold change.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Relative receptor frequency and absolute cell expansion differ; compatible counts and sampling are needed to infer the latter.
rows.entailment: Compatible absolute-cell counts are explicitly required to infer expansion rather than frequency change alone.
sourceScope: A denominator distinction, not a claim that sequencing proportions count cells directly.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: A peptide-stimulated mixture response is not automatically assigned to clone Q without linkage.
rows.entailment: The mixture peptide response is explicitly unlinked to Q and therefore cannot assign Q's specificity.
sourceScope: Fictional mixture assay; the response is not traced to a paired receptor or a naturally presenting tumour.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: First detection and a separate peptide response establish neither receptor rewriting, natural tumour recognition nor a clinical outcome comparison.
rows.entailment: The text withholds receptor creation, tumour killing and clinical benefit from first detection or an unlinked stimulation result.
sourceScope: Premise-backed inference; no receptor rewriting, natural recognition or outcome comparison was measured.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: The 0.1%, 1% and tenfold examples are invented assumptions with compatible methods and sampling, not clinical thresholds or patient observations.
rows.entailment: The final sentence identifies all three numbers as invented premises under comparable sampling and methods.
sourceScope: No patient observations, assay-performance estimates or treatment cutoffs are introduced.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: DNA, RNA and protein measurements address different biological layers.
rows.entailment: DNA, RNA and protein are explicitly different questions rather than interchangeable evidence.
sourceScope: Wells consortium inputs and downstream peptide/HLA/T-cell experiments, not a proof that every input produces a target.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: A vaccine source list requires alteration identity, tumour specificity and biological support before HLA matching and target selection.
rows.entailment: Alteration identity, tumour specificity and biological support are required before HLA matching, target selection and construction.
sourceScope: A source-list framework grounded in distinct inputs, not a validated target-scoring algorithm.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: A longer source list may add uncertain calls as well as genuine candidates.
rows.entailment: The paragraph explicitly states that adding candidates may add uncertain calls as well as real ones.
sourceScope: A logical reading rule about candidate lists, with no estimated false-positive rate.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Variant calling infers alterations from prepared molecules, aligned reads, a reference, support and competing explanations; it does not directly observe a complete tumour genome.
rows.entailment: The owner describes evidence assessment, a reference/comparison, quality, error models and bounded negatives, rather than direct observation of a complete genome.
sourceScope: Jones 2015 targeted/exome methods: aligned data, class-specific calling, stringent coverage/error criteria and manual candidate inspection.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Matched normal comparison helps distinguish inherited from acquired sequence findings.
rows.entailment: The paragraph conditions inherited/acquired attribution on adequate tumour and normal evidence.
sourceScope: Jones 2015 abstract and paired-analysis methods; no universal accuracy or automatic hereditary diagnosis.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: A somatic sequence change does not by itself establish malignancy, because acquired changes can occur in nonmalignant cells.
rows.entailment: The text explicitly includes normal tissues in somatic lineages and separates origin from harmfulness.
sourceScope: MedlinePlus origin/mosaicism paragraphs and Razavi 2019 abstract including controls without cancer; no claim that every blood variant is benign.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Normal-specimen suitability, sampling and contamination must be assessed.
rows.entailment: The note lists specimen identity, suitable normal, mismatch, contamination, low coverage and confirmation policy.
sourceScope: Jones comparison-sample limitations plus the bounded specimen-role interpretation; not a universal normal-sampling prescription.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Tumour-only analysis estimates some inherited/acquired distinctions but does not always establish them confidently.
rows.entailment: The text describes tumour-only attribution as inference from databases/fractions/models and explains why rare germline changes can remain unresolved.
sourceScope: Jones 2015 abstract and methods; numerical false-positive results remain specific to that study's pipelines.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: For tumour DNA, record call support, coverage, artefacts, tumour fraction and copy number.
rows.entailment: The tumour-DNA sentence explicitly records coverage, artefacts, tumour fraction and copy number with support.
sourceScope: Jones methods and Wong 2014 abstract; no universal minimum depth, purity or allele-fraction cutoff.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: For normal DNA, absence is conditional on the appropriate comparison, sampling and detection limits.
rows.entailment: The matched-normal sentence explicitly makes absence conditional on suitability, sampling, coverage and detection limits.
sourceScope: A bounded-negative reading rule with Jones paired-analysis context; adequately covered does not mean omniscient.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: For tumour RNA, assess altered transcript support, mixed-cell origin, expression depth and RNA processing.
rows.entailment: The RNA sentence names altered transcript support, mixed cells, expression depth and processing.
sourceScope: Wells distinct tumour RNA input and the guide's measurement framework; no cell-of-origin or translation guarantee from bulk RNA.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Protein or peptide detection needs method coverage, cell-of-origin and detection-limit context.
rows.entailment: The final sentence keeps protein/peptide method coverage, cell origin and detection limits separate from DNA/RNA evidence.
sourceScope: Wells binding and patient-matched T-cell validation are not a whole natural peptidome or clinical efficacy assay.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Targeted panels, whole exomes and whole genomes examine selected, largely coding and broader sequence territories respectively.
rows.entailment: The paragraph identifies panel territory, mostly coding exome enrichment and broader genome sampling.
sourceScope: MedlinePlus exome/genome definitions and Jones targeted/exome methods; intended territory is distinct from perfect coverage.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Greater sequencing breadth does not itself ensure sufficient depth, accurate structural calls or a useful antigen.
rows.entailment: It explicitly withholds automatic depth, reliable structural calls and useful antigen inference from breadth alone.
sourceScope: Workflow-specific scope reading, not a comparative platform-performance claim.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: VAF is a proportion of usable reads or assay-defined molecules supporting an allele at a specified locus.
rows.entailment: The existing note defines usable read or assay-molecule denominators at the alternate sequence.
sourceScope: Assay-defined fraction teaching; molecule-based values are not silently treated as read-based values.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Normal-cell admixture, local copy number and mutant-copy multiplicity affect VAF.
rows.entailment: The summary names purity, allele-specific copies, ploidy, mixture and assay behaviour as determinants of the value.
sourceScope: Carter 2012 abstract and targeted purity/ploidy/multiplicity text; no universal fit or conversion.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Read fraction is not automatically cancer-cell fraction; a half-read observation cannot be converted to half the cancer cells without purity, copy-number and multiplicity assumptions.
rows.entailment: The summary rejects direct conversion to a cancer-cell percentage and the model formula shows the missing assumptions. With pure diploid cancer and one altered copy per cell, 50% VAF is compatible with 100% carrier cancer cells.
sourceScope: The counterexample is algebra under the explicitly stated diploid-normal, uniform-copy, fixed-multiplicity and unbiased-observation assumptions, not clinical data.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Truncal ancestry across sampled branches differs from a subclone carried by only a subset of cancer cells.
rows.entailment: The text separates a sampled cancer-cell fraction from truncal ancestry across branches and subclonal membership.
sourceScope: Carter subclonal-model context and a definition-based ancestry reading rule, not a universal clinical clonality threshold.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: One small biopsy need not establish the alteration distribution across all sites.
rows.entailment: One small biopsy explicitly does not establish distribution across every site.
sourceScope: Sampling inference; unobserved sites are not assigned an alteration state.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Neither ancestry nor allele fraction demonstrates peptide display.
rows.entailment: The paragraph explicitly says that read fraction and ancestry do not demonstrate displayed peptide.
sourceScope: Genomic distribution and presentation are distinct evidence layers; no antigen-display frequency is inferred.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Invented candidate A has tumour DNA, adequate normal absence and mutant RNA; this is further evidence progression but not demonstrated presentation or T-cell recognition.
rows.entailment: Candidate A's DNA, assessed-normal absence and mutant RNA earn progress on source evidence but leave processing, display and recognition untested.
sourceScope: Invented candidate premises, not a validated clinical score or an observed patient.

rows.subject: data

rows.entailment: Candidate B's inadequate normal coverage explicitly leaves specificity unresolved.
sourceScope: Invented bounded-negative example, not a claim that every normal-negative variant is tumour-specific.

rows.subject: data

rows.entailment: The weak RNA-only junction in C explicitly needs reproducibility and artefact assessment.
sourceScope: Invented evidence gap; agreement on the same reads does not create independent molecular confirmation.

sourceScope: Invented sampling/sensitivity limitation, not a biological expression result.

sourceScope: Wong 2014 abstract supports fixation damage; Jones methods support mapping/error/manual checks. The Wong article body was not read.

sourceScope: A bounded sampling inference, not an estimated assay false-negative rate.
